third_party_cartridges.summary: No report found about this model rejecting third-party toner. Brother's Australian FAQ says a non-genuine cartridge should go to its maker or seller, and mentions no chip or firmware rule. Chip-equipped compatibles are sold in the UK and Europe, and Brother has denied in press reports that firmware blocks third-party toner, but I could not read that article in full.

windows.why: The only model-specific Windows and setup pages I could open are Brother's manual pages and the Which? listing; no owner reports about this model's Windows use were readable, and the scanning complaints I did read are about a sibling model.
windows.driver: Not verified. Brother's download list for this model did not render and third-party driver sites returned 403. Which? lists the model as compatible with Windows 10 and 11.
problems: Wi-Fi drop: the machine can disconnect from the wireless network; Brother's fix is Recover WLAN on the panel
Sibling DCP-L2550DW: wireless scanning stopped after a Windows 11 update, and the thread shows no confirmed fix
Brother's network repair step: check that the printer IP and subnet match the PC; Brother points to its Network Connection Repair Tool
windows.scanning: Flatbed (CIS) scanner with A4/Letter glass, no document feeder. Brother's Web Services guide (DCP-L family) adds the device on Windows via Control Panel > Add a device so it can scan over the network; it names no app and no account. The guide does not name this model, iPrint&Scan or Windows Scan, and USB scanning on Windows 11 is not verified.

sources.what: Web Services setup for installing the scanner driver on Windows 10 and 11 (DCP-L family manual); no account or app named
Lists DCP-L2620DW for Recover WLAN after a wireless drop; Network Connection Repair Tool for IP mismatch

forums.why: I could not read any owner opinions for this model: the review pages I opened had no reviews or were paywalled, and the Back Market, digitec and Amazon pages were blocked or timed out.
